correctness.rationale: Strict convexity and KKT subgradients are explicit. The internal flux on a proper fused block is a convex interpolation of its initial flux and exterior-boundary flux average. Uniform cycle penalties preserve every block for n>=4; triangle exterior signs are opposite, giving exactly the three mass-weighted inequalities. A violated local inequality yields a KKT-defined two-vertex fused datum and a later flux infeasibility after the initial fusion interval. Two exact rational witnesses validate concrete separations, without extrapolating sampled checks to universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full cyclic all-data classification by graph size is not logically implied by the inspected published graph-path algorithms, uniform-case boundary lemmas, or weighted-path results. New content is necessity of uniform penalties for every simple cycle with at least four vertices and the exact positive-mass triangle inequality including nonconstant stable examples. Literature and semantic comparisons were performed; remaining historical priority uncertainty is stated.
residual_risks: No research-record or literature index is exhaustive; an unindexed historical cycle-specific all-data criterion could predate this finding.
The broad generalized-lasso theoretical literature could encode an equivalent converse in a non-obvious matrix reduction, although no such implication was identified in inspected material.

value.rationale: A complete all-data parameter classification makes permanent contraction of fused graph nodes mathematically safe exactly in the permitted regions. The graph-size discontinuity at n=4 is structural, and the nonconstant stable triangle plus arbitrarily asymmetric masses distinguish it from a routine restatement of the path result. The counterexample mechanism is constructive, not a tiny numerical gain.
